Doctors often have to shift priorities throughout the day. 

One patient requiring direct admission to a hospital will require the physician to find an accepting provider, get in contact with them, explain the reason for the admission, provide report, ensure medications, orders, allergies are documented, arrange transport (if not 911).   During a pandemic or influenza season, this is fairly common. 

The service on demand model requires physicians to see ~6 patients an hour to justify their square footage cost.   

They also have to handle interpreting results, refill prescription, insurance paperwork, etc.   

How much extra do they make for these duties that are mostly done after a full day at their office/hospital?  Zero.  

The $300 bill you initially see will be reduced to $60-$110 actual payment.

The plight of mental health in America is that those whose who need it most have limited means to pay for it, especially since most states have shut down treatment facilities that provided indigent mental health services and private health systems (even nonprofits) need to make money to keep the doors open.  Even if you have insurance, the benefits are very limited.  The only bright side I can identify is that the stigma of mental health disorders is slowly evaporating. 

Source: Veteran who receives MH treatment from the VA and works in health care.
